sources.title: A family of embedded Runge-Kutta formulae
sources.read_scope: Publisher metadata via Exa; coefficients cross-checked with Hairer/Wanner original DOPRI5 implementation.
limits: No claim of new DOPRI coefficients.

sources.title: DOPRI5 Fortran source
sources.read_scope: Full source text retrieved via Exa; stage coefficients, FSAL handoff, rejection, norm and stiffness heuristic inspected.
supports: Exact rational tableau and error coefficients
Six new RHS evaluations per full attempt after initial RHS
limits: Current Rust driver is a new integration of these formulas, not a byte-for-byte port or certification by original authors.

sources.title: Parallel iteration of high-order Runge-Kutta methods with stepsize control
sources.read_scope: Author institute full manuscript retrieved via Exa; sections1–2 on explicit predictor-corrector iterations and RHS-dominated cost assumptions inspected.
supports: Parallel stage iterations can construct high-order explicit methods
Implicit corrector stability is not inherited by a finite explicit iteration
Work and sequential RHS depth are distinct costs
limits: Published hardware and methods do not establish VigilODE speedup; q4-DOPRI construction here is derived for the present tableau.

sources.title: A comparison of high-order explicit Runge-Kutta, extrapolation, and deferred correction methods in serial and parallel
sources.read_scope: Publisher and author arXiv abstract/metadata, independently found by SciSpace and Exa.
supports: Parallel extrapolation and deferred correction are relevant alternatives
Efficiency depends on order, tolerance and parallel execution
limits: Published N-body result is not reused as a VigilODE benchmark.

sources.title: Fortran Codes: Nonstiff Differential Equations
supports: DOPRI5 fifth-order endpoint and fourth-order dense output are distinct
DOP853 and ODEX are further established nonstiff routes
limits: New endpoint-landing API does not inherit a dense extension merely by using DOPRI5 coefficients.

searches.question: What are the original Dormand and Prince fifth-order embedded Runge-Kutta formulas with first-same-as-last derivative reuse, and what established parallel explicit Runge-Kutta or extrapolation methods reduce sequential stages for nonstiff differential equations?
searches.metadata_correction: The two records for Ketcheson/Waheed are duplicates; publisher confirms journal year2014, not repository-record year2022.

searches.question: Original Dormand-Prince formula, Hairer DOPRI5 source and parallel iterated Runge-Kutta primary literature

How does the 1980 paper A family of embedded Runge-Kutta formulae by J. R. Dormand and P. J. Prince construct its fifth-order embedded method, and how do Runge-Kutta-Chebyshev methods extend explicit stability for diffusion-type mildly stiff systems?
searches.use: Exploratory scope only; returned stabilized-method abstracts informed future candidate search, not a new implementation claim.
